facts.text: The gantry sends G-code through printer.gcode.script and reads motion state through printer.objects.query
get_target_position queries gcode_move and returns its position keyed by axis_map
get_current_position queries motion_report and returns live_position indexed X, Y, Z and E
The gantry module sets MIN_STEPPER_CURRENT = 0.10, MAX_STEPPER_CURRENT = 1.00, DEFAULT_MOVE_TIMEOUT = 180.0, POSITION_TOLERANCE = 0.001 and DEFAULT_MOVE_SPEED = 20.0
wait_for_move polls the live position until every tracked axis is within the tolerance or the timeout expires
Gantry.move sends the XY move and the Z move as separate G0 commands and waits after each
home() sends G28 (or SET_KINEMATIC_POSITION X=0 Y=0 Z=0 when debug is true) and raises MotionError when the reply is not 'ok'
enable_motors sends M17 and disable_motors sends M18
get_status reads printer.info and returns its 'state' value
is_connected is true only while the Moonraker WebSocket is open
The gantry and deck configuration express distances in millimetres (_mm keys) with a default speed of 100 mm/s
The bring-up guide tells the operator to keep a hand near the power switch or emergency stop before any motion
The example printer configuration wires the x_max and y_max switches to M112, an emergency stop
The guide says the example travel limits and driver currents must be reviewed against the actual machine and are a starting point, not a substitute for calibration
